recentItems.title: Aftermath of powerful blast at Athens' tourist district
recentItems.description:
(25 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Athens, Greece - 25 September 2026
1. Wide of site of explosion with first responders on scene and the Acropolis seen in the background
2. Greek flag on Acropolis with tourists surrounding it
3. Wide of debris in street with first responders at scene
4. Reverse of man wearing high visibility vest with text identifying a natural gas works company 
5. Wide of building damaged by the explosion with first responders and natural gas works company employees at scene
6. Wide of Giotis Kantartzis, pastor of the First Greek Evangelical Church in Athens speaking with media
7. Wide of lettering identifying church and broken windows
8. Various of cross above entrance and broken windows
9. SOUNDBITE (Greek) Giotis Kantartzis, pastor of the First Greek Evangelical Church in Athens:
"A lot of damage. There is a lot of damage, but once again, what matters most to us is that everyone who was inside got out safely. That's the main thing. That's most important."
10. Pan of broken windows
11. SOUNDBITE (Greek) Giotis Kantartzis, pastor of the First Greek Evangelical Church in Athens:
"Of course we went in (to the church). It was heartbreaking. From the bottom to the top, there is no window that has not been broken."
12. Wide of site of explosion with natural gas company workers digging
13. Close of worker digging
14. Close of building where explosion took place
15. Tracking shot of damaged car being removed from scene
16. Various of firefighters spraying water at damaged building
17. Damaged building
18. Various of police officers at scene
19. Mid of debris on damaged car
20. Wide of scene of explosion
STORYLINE:
A powerful blast shook the Greek capital’s tourist district of Plaka, near the ancient Acropolis, on Friday morning, causing a building to collapse and injuring at least two people who had to be rescued from an adjacent building, authorities said. 

The fire department said the explosion occurred in an old two-story building in the Plaka district, the historic part of Athens that lies at the foot of the Acropolis hill, Greece’s most visited ancient monument. 

Police cordoned off the area, while specialist fire department rescue crews with a sniffer dog were deployed to check whether any more people might be trapped. 

Local media reported that up to five people may have been inside the building at the time of the blast, but there was no confirmation.

The fire department said the search and rescue operation was still ongoing several hours after the explosion. 

The pastor for a nearby church said this Sunday's service would be held outdoors due to damage to the church from the explosion.  

“Of course we went in. It was heartbreaking. From the bottom to the top, there is no window that has not been broken,” said Giotis Kantartzis, pastor of the First Greek Evangelical Church in Athens.

Video footage from the scene showed rubble strewn across the street, with parked cars smashed by falling debris.

The cause of the explosion was not immediately clear, but local media said a gas leak was suspected.

AP Video by Lefteris Pitarakis
Production by Theodora Tongas

recentItems.title: Russian drone strike kills 14-year-old boy in Kyiv as attacks hit eight Ukrainian regions
recentItems.description:
(25 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Kyiv, Ukraine — 25 September 2026
1. Various of black smoke rising over the city
2. Rescuers carrying body of a teenage boy killed during strike
3. Various of rescue teams cleaning debris
4. Damaged residential building
5. Resident assisted to walk through debris
6. Various of emergency services at site
7. Close fragment of a missile
8. Various of residents
9. Various of dog on site, with residents
10. SOUNDBITE (English) Mykyta Sysuev, Kyiv resident:
"When I got into the hallway, everything, I understood everything immediately, because basically everything was gone. There were no doors, no windows. Everything is broken, glass lying everywhere. So I understood it's a tragedy. After that, I decided to check the news and find out that one of my neighbors has died. It was a teen, a teenager."
11. Men dismantling broken window
12. SOUNDBITE (English) Mykyta Sysuev, Kyiv resident: 
"The intensity of attacks has definitely increased and that's the most problematic thing right now, because the reactive drones, they are basically much faster than the different ones, the Shahed ones, the previous. And we are yet to find the solution to, so our anti-missile system could work with it, and we could find a cheap solution to strike it down before they hit somewhere in the city, buildings and kill people and so forth. And that's the most problematic thing."
13. Various of rescue teams at site
14. SOUNDBITE (Ukrainian) Nadia Alekseeva, pensioner from Kyiv: 
"Russian society is sick, it is simply sick, just as German society was sick when it had such a terrible leader as Hitler. Russian society is sick today as well. It simply does not understand what it is doing.”
15. Resident looking through broken window
16. Wide of damaged residential building
17. Emergency worker cleaning debris
18. SOUNDBITE (Ukrainian) Nadia Alekseeva, pensioner from Kyiv: 
"I do not see the end оf the war. І believe that the president of such a powerful country as the United States could intervene more actively and impose conditions on Russia so that it stops the delivery of weapons to the army. So that it withdraws from our territory. But that is impossible to predict at this point.”
19. Various of emergency worker at site
STORYLINE:
A 14-year-old boy was killed and at least seven people were injured when a Russian drone struck a 16-story residential building Friday in Kyiv’s Pecherskyi district around 8 a.m., according to the city’s military administration and police. 

The drone hit the building’s 10th and 11th floors.

Mykyta Sysuev, 23, a neighbor of the boy who was killed, recalled the aftermath of the attack.

“There were no doors, no windows. Everything was broken, with glass lying everywhere,” he said. 

Sysuev said he later checked the news and learned that his teenage neighbor had been killed. 

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said eight regions came under attack overnight. 

Russian authorities, meanwhile, said Ukrainian long-range strikes killed one person and wounded 21 others.

Nadia Alekseeva, an 88-year-old Kyiv pensioner, said she could not foresee an end to the war and urged the United States to take a more active role in pressuring Russia to withdraw from Ukrainian territory.

AP video shot by Srdjan Nedeljkovic and Volodymyr Yurchuk

recentItems.title: Fears of renewed fighting in Ethiopia as internet and transport services halt
recentItems.description:
(25 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Mekelle, Ethiopia - 24 September 2026


1. Various of street scenes and local market in Mekelle
2. SOUNDBITE (Tigrinya) Selam Fantay, Mekelle resident:

++STARTS ON SHOT 1 AND IS OVERLAID BY SHOT 3++
"There is an atmosphere of fear. People are deeply concerned that the suspension of transport services signals the outbreak of renewed conflict.” 
3. Various of activity at local market
4. SOUNDBITE (Tigrinya) Hailay Meles, Mekelle resident: 

++STARTS ON SHOT 3 AND IS OVERLAID BY SHOT 5++
"The country is at war, and peace remains elusive as transport services have come to a halt. As long as this conflict persists, it will continue to drive up the prices of basic commodities.” 
5. Various wide of street scenes
6. SOUNDBITE (Tigrinya) Selam Fantay, Mekelle resident:

++STARTS ON SHOT 5 AND IS OVERLAID BY SHOT 7++
"Without peace, everything becomes extremely difficult. Our desire is for peace to return so that conditions can be created where everyone can work and earn a living. Peace is the top priority — that is what we truly want.” 
7. Various of activity at local market
8. SOUNDBITE (Tigrinya) Hailay Meles, Mekelle resident:

++STARTS ON SHOT 7 AND IS OVERLAID BY SHOT 9++ 
"I hope for a peaceful resolution to this conflict. It seems the international community is ignoring our situation, opting instead for silence. Yet, as history has shown that war solves nothing, the international community has to intervene and help resolve this crisis.” 
9. Various of street scenes and local market in Mekelle
STORYLINE:
Internet service was disrupted across parts of northern Ethiopia on Friday as renewed fighting between Tigrayan fighters and the Ethiopian federal troops heightened fears of another prolonged conflict.

The fighting has shattered a peace pact that ended a devastating two-year war in 2022, as rebel forces mobilized for an armed struggle they hope will lead to the removal of the federal prime minister.

Internet monitoring group NetBlocks said network data indicated a regional disruption corresponding with reports of a telecommunications blackout in Tigray. 

A day earlier, residents of the Tigray capital, Mekelle, described an atmosphere of fear and warned that disrupted transport links could increase the cost of basic goods.

"The country is at war and peace remains elusive as transport services have come to a halt. As long as this conflict persists, it will continue to drive up the prices of basic commodities,” said Hailay Meles, a resident.

The main combatants are Ethiopian federal troops and fighters loyal to the Tigray People’s Liberation Front, or TPLF, an armed political group in Tigray, Ethiopia's northernmost regional state.

Ethiopia's military said Thursday that dozens of TPLF fighters had been killed in ongoing operations and that federal forces “have been able to detain many” others and seize a large quantity of weapons from them.

The TPLF and Ethiopian federal troops waged war between November 2020 and November 2022, when a peace deal was signed in Pretoria, South Africa.

"I hope for a peaceful resolution to this conflict. It seems the international community is ignoring our situation, opting instead for silence," said Meles.

recentItems.title: Full results from Russia's parliamentary election confirm Kremlin's dominance
recentItems.description:
(25 Sep 2026) 
++PLEASE NOTE: AP IS OPERATING IN RUSSIA ACCORDING TO RUSSIAN RESTRICTIONS ON ALL REPORTING RELATED TO THE ONGOING MILITARY OPERATION IN UKRAINE++

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Moscow, Russia -  25 September 2026
1. Wide of Head of Russia’s Central Election Commission Ella Pamfilova preparing for briefing
2. Wide of briefing 
3. SOUNDBITE (Russian) Ella Pamfilova, head of Russia’s Central Election Commission:
++INCLUDES PAN RIGHT TO SHOW RESULTS ON SCREEN++
"United Russia secured 349 seats: 140 from the federal constituency and 209 from single-mandate constituencies. The Communist Party of the Russian Federation won 37 seats: 32 from the federal constituency and five from single-mandate constituencies. The LDPR (Liberal Democratic Party of Russia) took 23 seats: 21 from the federal constituency and two from single-mandate constituencies. The New People party won 19 seats, all from the federal constituency. A Just Russia secured 17 seats: 13 from the federal constituency and four from single-mandate constituencies. The Rodina party won one seat, and four seats went to independent candidates."
4. Audience
5. SOUNDBITE (Russian) Ella Pamfilova, head of Russia’s Central Election Commission:
"As has been noted repeatedly, this campaign differed significantly from all previous ones - and certainly from the similar campaign held under peaceful conditions in 2021 - primarily because it took place amidst an escalation of unprecedented and multifaceted threats. I believe we all felt this. It is also highly significant that, for the first time, our fellow citizens from the four reunited constituent entities of the Russian Federation - the Donetsk and Luhansk People's Republics and the Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions - participated in the State Duma elections."
6. Various of briefing
7. SOUNDBITE (Russian) Ella Pamfilova, head of Russia’s Central Election Commission:
"For the first time, 46 participants or veterans of the special military operation were elected — representing, in effect, over 10% of the total number of seats."
8. Wide of briefing
STORYLINE:
Russian authorities on Friday released the full results from the country's first wartime parliamentary election, which further cemented the Kremlin's overwhelming political control.

According to the results released by the Central Election Commission, the main Kremlin party, United Russia, will get more than three-fourths of the seats in the lower house, the State Duma, a record high. 

The tightly orchestrated vote excluded virtually any genuine opposition.

Nearly 60% of the 111 million eligible voters turned out in the three-day balloting that ended Sunday, the most for a parliamentary election. 

Authorities had spread the voting over three days and allowed online voting in some regions to boost participation.

The parliamentary election was the first since President Vladimir Putin launched the military operation in Ukraine in 2022, and the first to include residents of four regions of that country that were seized and illegally annexed by Moscow later that year.

Voting also was held in Crimea, which was taken by Russia in 2014. 

Kyiv denounced the voting in those regions as illegal.

Putin declared Wednesday that the election results were a show of public support for the Kremlin's policies.

A massive state media campaign and tight control over the election allowed the Kremlin to strengthen its political dominance despite economic troubles and long-range Ukrainian drone attacks.

Central Election Commission chief Ella Pamfilova said that United Russia got 349 out of 450 Duma seats.

recentItems.title: UNRWA's future in Gaza uncertain amid quiet talks with Board of Peace
recentItems.description:
(25 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY: 

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
ARCHIVE: Gaza City, Gaza Strip - 15 October 2025
1. Aerial shot showing destruction

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Geneva - 24 September 2026
++ZOOM INTERVIEW++
++QUALITY AS INCOMING++
++NAME OVERLAID ON VIDEO++
2. SOUNDBITE (English) Philippe Lazzarini, the former commissioner-General of the UNRWA (the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestinian Refugees): ++SOUNDBITE OVERLAID ON SHOTS 1-4++
"It is true now that, you know, we... there is no other choice than to partner with the Board of Peace. UN agencies are doing this, but by doing this, they also contribute further, I would say, further push UNRWA out of the equation, despite the renewal of its mandate and the expectation of the people on the ground that the agency continues to play a key role."

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Gaza City, Gaza Strip - 24 September 2026
3. Pan of camp of displaced people, destroyed buildings in background 
4. Camp with destroyed buildings in background

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Geneva - 24 September 2026
++ZOOM INTERVIEW++
++QUALITY AS INCOMING++
5. SOUNDBITE (English) Philippe Lazzarini, the former commissioner-General of the UNRWA (the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestinian Refugees): ++SOUNDBITE OVERLAID ON SHOTS 6-11 ++
"If everyone stopped working today, public health would further collapse. It's already in a bad shape, it's already at level of deep concern, but what's being kept and maintained would definitely collapse. We still represent that I would say more than half of the entire public health in Gaza Strip."

ASSOCIATED PRESS
ARCHIVE: Gaza City, Gaza Strip - 15 October 2025
9. Aerial showing destruction across Gaza City, people walking, cars driving
10. Aerial showing destruction
11. Various of camps, destroyed building at the background

ASSOCIATED PRESS
ARCHIVE: Jerusalem - 18 May 2026
12. UNRWA banner on ground among debris

STORYLINE:
The former commissioner-general of the U.N. agency for Palestinian refugees has said that UNRWA has "no other choice than to partner with" the U.S.-created Board of Peace in Gaza Strip. 

Philippe Lazzarini, who was head of UNRWA until earlier this year, told The Associated Press that members of the technocratic committee want to work with the agency. 

UNRWA remains the territory’s largest aid provider, playing a key role in health and education even though Israel wants it out of Gaza and has repeatedly accused the agency of being infiltrated by Hamas militants, allegations that the International Court of Justice says have not been substantiated. 

Another U.N. official shared with AP minutes from meetings where UNRWA and the committee discussed collaborating on plans for Gaza.

A Board of Peace official confirmed that board members had met multiple times with UNRWA officials. 

The agency’s days are over, the official said, speaking on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to talk to the media. 

There’s been no reconstruction in Gaza, almost a year since the ceasefire. 

Israel still prevents the entry of the Palestinian committee chosen by the Board of Peace to eventually govern the strip, saying Hamas must first disarm. 

The Board says it can activate its plans for Gaza in earnest once the committee gets inside the strip.

That's left UNRWA on the ground in Gaza, with far more workers than any other U.N. agency or nongovernmental organization.

It props up about half of Gaza’s public health system, said Lazzarini, whose last working day was March 31. He plans to publish a book this year about his tenure.

recentItems.title: Israelis offer mixed reactions to Netanyahu’s speech at the United Nations
recentItems.description:
(25 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Jerusalem - 25 September 2026
1. Wide of people walking at market 
2. Mid of market fruit shop 
3. Wide of market 
4. SOUNDBITE (Hebrew) Shlomo Khuta, Jerusalem resident:
"I think, in my opinion, Bibi (Benjamin) Netanyahu's speech was excellent. It did good for the State of Israel, strengthened our policy, and only did good for the people of Israel and all its inhabitants."
5. Various of market
6. SOUNDBITE (Hebrew) Eyal Cohen Yashar, Jerusalem resident:
"Unfortunately, the speech by the leader of the State of Israel today was more for domestic purposes than for external propaganda. There's nothing left to convince, as the images speak for themselves and there's nothing we can do against it, the disaster that happened in Gaza."
7. Mid of a man carrying a gun
8. SOUNDBITE (Hebrew) Eyal Cohen Yashar, Jerusalem resident:
"From an economic standpoint, it is essential to have good relations with Turkey, even if they are not entirely right. Regarding Qatar, there is some truth to it, as historically Qatar has indeed funded many things in the Gaza Strip, not for the benefit of the residents, which is the most important thing."
9. Various of people shopping
10. SOUNDBITE (Hebrew) Daniel Dvash, Jerusalem resident:
"I watched the entire speech. The speech was good, in my opinion. He mainly addressed the people in Israel and not those living abroad, not in the United States or in Europe. He simply wants to gain more mandates because he saw he was in trouble."
11. Various of people at a restaurant 
12. Various of market
13. Various of police outside the market
STORYLINE:
Israelis expressed mixed reactions on Friday to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's speech to the United Nations General Assembly, with some praising his defence of Israel's policies and others questioning his ability to sway international opinion.

Shlomo Khuta, a Jerusalem resident, said Netanyahu's address on Thursday had strengthened Israel's position.

"Netanyahu's speech was excellent. It did good for the State of Israel, strengthened our policy," he said.

Another Jerusalem resident, Eyal Cohen Yashar, said Netanyahu had failed to convince the international community over Israel's actions in Gaza.

"There's nothing left to convince, as the images speak for themselves and there's nothing we can do against it, the disaster that happened in Gaza," he said.

In his UNGA address, Netanyahu dismissed allegations of genocide in Gaza as "the biggest lie of the century" and defended Israel's military actions against Iran. 

Scores of delegates walked out of the assembly hall in protest as he took the podium.

The speech came amid mounting international criticism of Israel's military campaign in Gaza, launched in response to the Hamas-led attacks on October 7, 2023.

Netanyahu faces reelection next month in polls widely seen as a referendum on his responsibility for the security failures surrounding the attacks and his ability to defend Israel's reputation on the world stage.

AP Video by Shlomo Mor

recentItems.title: Church bells toll in Paris to mark the arrival of Pope Leo XIV in France amid increased security
recentItems.description:
(25 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Paris, France -  25 September 2026
1. Various of sunrise over Notre-Dame cathedral 
2. Various of bells ringing over Notre-Dame cathedral 
3. Various of police securing the area for Pope Leo XIV's drive in the popemobile 
4.  Marie Sophie Monestes and her husband arriving at the area to watch Pope driving in popemobile 
5. Tilt up of t-shirt 
6. SOUNDBITE (French) Marie Sophie Monestes, Catholic faithful:
"We have arrived at 7:30 a.m. to be the first for the Pope's route, to see the Pope in person. It's the first time I will see the Pope. I'm very happy to be here."
7. Various of volunteers setting up banners for Pope's visit
8. Military patrolling
9. Artistic director Solene Rousseau watching people setting up large white cloth
10. Close of a man on balcony
11. SOUNDBITE (French) Solene Rousseau, artistic director:
"He projects something that could bring peace in the chaos we are living in, reconciliation and joy. I think Pope Leo can take part in changing this world."  
12. Various of police dogs sniffing area for explosives
STORYLINE:
The sun rose over Paris’ Notre Dame Cathedral and its famous bells rang out for several minutes to mark Pope Leo XIV's arrival in France for a four-day visit on Friday.

In fact, church bells across France tolled when Leo’s charter flight landed at Paris’ Orly airport, and upward of a million people are expected to turn out to see him during his visit. The welcome has underscored the surprising level of interest in Pope Leo’s visit, the first by a pope in 18 years.

Even before Leo was greeted by French President Macron, police, bomb squads and military fanned out along Paris’ Left Bank, securing the perimeter of the route the Pope will take in his popemobile Friday afternoon as he makes his way through the crowded public to Notre Dame cathedral.

Olympic-level security measures have been put in place, including mounted police, bomb disposal experts, anti-drone and counter-terrorism measures, said Paris police prefecture spokesperson Hélène Denéchère.

In Paris alone, plans called for 14,000 police officers, gendarmes, and military personnel and 2,500 firefighters on Friday. On Saturday, when Leo celebrates Mass at the central Place de la Concorde, the numbers are only slightly lower.

“We are implementing a system similar to what was in place during the Paris 2024 Olympic and Paralympic Games, which means a protective perimeter around which other security perimeters will be added,” Denéchère said.

AP Video by Kostya Manenkov and Alex Turnbull
Produced by Jeffrey Schaeffer

recentItems.title: Pope Leo speaks to reporters as he flies from Rome to Paris
recentItems.description:
(25 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTIONS SUMMARY:

ASSOCIATED PRESS
In Air - 25 September 2026
1. Mid of Pope Leo speaking to reporters

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Paris - 25 September 2026
2. Wide of officials waiting to greet Pope Leo at Paris Orly International Airport
3. SOUNDBITE (English) Nicole Winfield, The Associated Press:
"Pope Leo has welcomed reporters on his plane and said he welcomes good coverage of his trips. This was after he was asked by a CNN reporter about the Trump administration's decision to try to bar CNN and some other news organizations. Leo has frequently spoken out about the need for a free and independent press, and he affirmed that today on his way to France. He came to the back of the plane, and he was asked about this ban and whether he had some words to those colleagues who have been kept out of the White House. And he reaffirmed that there is a need for a good coverage everywhere and for everyone."
4. Wide of plane with officials in foreground 
STORYLINE:
Pope Leo XIV told reporters they were welcome to cover him, as he responded to the Trump administration’s attempt to bar U.S. media from the White House and affirmed the importance of journalists covering public figures.

Leo spoke to reporters Friday on his way to France for a four-day visit. Asked by a CNN reporter about the Trump administration’s attempt to bar CNN and other reporters, Leo said the media was welcome on his plane.

“I am very happy that here, you are all welcome,” he said. "Good media coverage is important, he said, and equally important "that we have it all the way around, for everyone”

CNN, MS NOW and Politico were back at the White House on Thursday after a judge handed them a reprieve from President Donald Trump's ban, but the extraordinary showdown between him and outlets whose coverage he dislikes continued.

On a high-profile day when Chinese leader Xi Jinping was visiting Washington and attending a state dinner, no major American network aired live coverage, and both CNN and MS NOW said their journalists were denied access to Xi’s state dinner arrival. 

Leo has long affirmed the need for free and independent press, a point he made in one of his first audiences as pope. 

Speaking to journalists who covered the 2025 conclave that elected him, the American pope called for the release of imprisoned journalists and affirmed the “precious gift of free speech and the press.” 

That said, since the COVID-19 pandemic, independent media have been prevented from covering photo opportunities inside the pope's private studio when visiting heads of state meet with the pontiff. 

Additionally, many of the pope's private audiences with other groups and individuals are closed to non-Vatican press.

On the flight Friday, Leo also apologized for missing an opportunity to speak with the press the last time he traveled internationally, when his Iberia charter broke down in Spain's Canary Islands and he returned home solo on the king's private jet, skipping his traditional airborne press conference with reporters.

More than 70 reporters and the Vatican delegation waited for several hours at the airport for a replacement plane to arrive. 

Leo addressed the media's disappointment when he came to the back of the plane to greet reporters.

“A special mention I would like to make for those of you who were traveling with me when we returned to Rome from Spain,” he said. “I want to apologize personally for an incident, that I had nothing to do with, but which I know left a number of you unhappy with the fact that we couldn’t have the flight back together back to Rome.”
